description: Site: lib.rs:1115-1130. Code intent: O(1) by-id lookup via HashMap. Actual code: HashMap<&'static str, Option<Box<dyn Lint>>>, then by_id.keys().copied().find(|k| *k == id.as_str()) for each id in the input slice. This is O(n) per lookup, O(n*m) overall (n = registered lints, m = requested ids). The HashMap itself is never used as a hashmap. The comment explains 'lifetime juggling — by_id keys are &static str but id is a runtime String, so we lift the lookup through the borrow' — but the fix is simply by_id.get(id.as_str()): &str implements Borrow<str> for HashMap<&'static str, _> lookup, so id.as_str() (&str) is a valid key against keys that are &'static str. The current code is over-careful and slow. Filter_to_ids on the typical OSCAL Catalog round-trip is fine at today's lint counts (~10-50), but becomes meaningful when pkix-policy-zlint lands and runs against ~700 zlint lints.
title: LintRunner::filter_to_ids does O(n) linear scan inside HashMap lookup, defeating the HashMap
